revision: 1. Keep the planet as the visual hero but shift or reduce it slightly so the left column forms a tight title → mission brief → Start Mission sequence, with the button directly following the brief and clearly dominating other actions. 2. Resolve the start-screen state: label the top HUD as an upcoming Wave 07 forecast and projected core condition, or reset it to pre-launch values; do not imply an already-running match. 3. Expand the bottom loadout into three readable, equally constructed Damage, Fire Rate, and Speed action cards with functional icons/micro-visualizations, current level, credit cost, and an explicit Upgrade/Select affordance; align the Loadout heading and keep a bottom safe area. 4. Refine rather than replace the planet: sharpen vector landmasses, atmospheric rim, shadow, and orbital geometry; normalize stroke weights, title contrast, secondary-copy legibility, and particle clipping within the existing cyan/blue/magenta command system. Add one restrained enemy trajectory or shield-stress cue to connect mission threat to the planet.
conflicts: The planet should remain the memorable centerpiece, but the start action must be operationally primary; retain the planet's scale while opening enough left-column space for a continuous launch flow.
Expressive, distinct upgrades are useful, but per-card decoration could fragment the system; differentiate them through functional icons and data within one card template.
The populated HUD builds game context but contradicts a start state; reinterpret it explicitly as mission forecast rather than removing requested metrics.
rationale: I preserved the strong defense-console identity while making launch state and upgrade actions unambiguous, using semantic variation inside one disciplined HUD system.
audit_note: Central moderation authored from the task brief, shared r0 screenshot, and all four shared axis critiques only. No FUSED or MAD outputs, generated revisions, HTML variants, or scores were inspected.
